english.title: Care worker ill-treat / wilfully neglect an individual
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) having the care of **(..SPECIFY NAME OF VICTIM..) by virtue of being a care worker, ill-treated or wilfully neglected

(A)_[him]_
(B)_[her]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 20(1) and (2) of the Criminal Justice and Courts Act 2015.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
having the care of another
by virtue of being a care worker
ill-treated / wilfully neglected that individual

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) For the purposes of this offence, care worker means an individual who, as paid work, provides -
(a) health care for an adult or child, other than excluded health care, or
(b) social care for an adult,
including an individual who, as paid work, supervises or manages individuals providing such care or is a director or similar officer of an organisation which provides such care.
(ii) Further definitions of terms used can be found in section 20(4) - (8)

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months imprisonment and / or a fine
Indictment: Five years imprisonment and / or a fine

Note:
In relation to an offence committed before paragraph 24(2) of Schedule 22 to the Sentencing Act 2020 comes into force (01/12/20), the reference to 12 months imprisonment in relation to summary offences, above, is to be read as a reference to 6 months imprisonment.

Time Limit For Prosecutions:
None
